title: Keg Carbonation Pressure-to-Temperature Check
dataSources: Fermentation telemetry (`brew:fermentation`), brew-day records (`brew:batch`), mash probes (`brew:mash`), keg pressure (`kegerator:pressure`), tap pours (`kegerator:pour`), brew-fridge duty logs (`brewfridge:compressor`), cellar climate (`winecellar:reading`), and line-cleaning events (`tapline:clean`).
app: Homebrewing telemetry from Tilt/iSpindel fermentation sensors, Brewfather batch exports, ESPHome mash and fridge probes, keg pressure sensors, tap flow meters, and cellar climate sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=kegerator:pressure
| stats latest(pressure_psi) as pressure_psi latest(temp_c) as temp_c by keg tap
| eval pressure_temp_ratio=round(pressure_psi/(temp_c+0.1),1)
| sort - pressure_temp_ratio
description: Reviews keg pressure alongside serving temperature so over- and under-carbonated pours stand out quickly.
value: Carbonation problems often come from the pressure and temperature combination, and this check turns that relationship into a simple ranking.
implementation: Send keg regulator and kegerator temperature readings to Splunk and compare taps after line changes or gas adjustments.
visualization: Table of keg pressure, serving temperature, and relative carbonation ratio.
grandmaExplanation: It maps whether each keg's gas pressure matches how cold it is, so pours stay closer to the carbonation you want.
